summary: Chat-alignment fix verified end-to-end for conversation dc1cf7d7 as mei@demo.com at 320/360/390/430. All outgoing bubbles hug the right edge with an equal 16px margin, long outgoing bubbles never cross the left avatar column (left-edge always >= padding+40), incoming rows share a consistent left edge (avatar column + gap), the outgoing Voice Call event card sits at the same right edge as outgoing text bubbles, and there is no horizontal overflow at any of the 4 widths. WS-keepalive regression: the call-signaling WebSocket stayed open for the full 60s observation window and emitted 2 client->server ping frames (~25s cadence) with no repeated close/reopen loop. Full 2-context WebRTC audio-call and voice-room regressions were NOT re-executed here — iterations 23 and 25 already verified those flows browser-to-browser and the agent-to-agent note explicitly said real-device audio cannot be verified in the web preview. A minor separate finding: the chat-list WebSocket in use-chat-socket.ts has no client ping, so it will drop after the ingress idle timeout and reconnect after 3s; call signaling is unaffected.

ws_keepalive.note: Chat-list WS (use-chat-socket.ts) has no client ping and closed once in the same window; auto-reconnects after 3s. Not the WS mentioned in the review request but worth reporting.

action_items: Optional: add a client-side ping (e.g. every 25s) inside use-chat-socket.ts mirroring the CallContext keepalive so the chat WS doesn't get idle-closed by the ingress every ~60s.

The measurement script currently picks up partner-intro chips as candidate bubbles because they share the same rounded-background heuristic. If you want future automation to be exact, add data-testid=chat-bubble to the bubble Pressable and data-testid=chat-call-card to callCard so the DOM query is deterministic.
critical_code_review_comments: chat/[id].tsx callRowTheirs marginLeft is 40 + spacing.sm (48px). Combined with messageList padding (spacing.lg = 16) that puts every incoming callCard at x=64 — identical to the incoming bubble start (padding 16 + avatarWrap 40 + row gap spacing.sm 8 = 64). That is the exact alignment the user reported was previously broken, and it is now correct at all widths tested.
callCard has minWidth 170 + maxWidth 100% + flexShrink 1; at 320px width that still fits inside the 86% callRow (275px), no clipping seen.
use-chat-socket.ts is missing a keepalive ping — not blocking but recommended to align with CallContext WS behaviour.
seed_data_creation: None — used the pre-seeded conversation dc1cf7d7-2f98-43dc-8a15-07b8ff742e03 and demo users mei@demo.com / diego@demo.com.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two-context WebRTC audio-call (fake-media Chromium args) and voice-room mesh flow were NOT re-executed this iteration; iterations 23/25 verified them and this run focused on the alignment bug + WS ping regression. If a full call regression is needed again, reuse /app/test_reports/iter23_e2e_call.py + iter23_room_smoke.py. To re-run alignment, run /app/test_reports/iter27_chat_alignment.py logic via mcp_browser_automation (the script uses page.evaluate to measure bounding rects at 4 widths).
rca_of_issue: Previous bug: incoming Voice Call event cards were rendered inside a container without the callRowTheirs marginLeft, so they started at x = list_padding (16px) instead of x = list_padding + avatar_col_width + gap (64px), i.e. 48px to the LEFT of the neighbouring incoming text bubbles. Fix (verified): callRowTheirs now applies marginLeft: 40 + spacing.sm (48px), which added on top of the 16px list padding places incoming call cards at the same x=64 as incoming text bubbles. Outgoing call cards use alignSelf:'flex-end' which keeps them flush with the outgoing bubble right edge (16px inside viewport). Measurements at 320/360/390/430 all confirm equal 16px right margins for every outgoing bubble and no left-edge violation.
